🇺🇸 SEPTEMBER FOMC SUMMARY: • The economy has strengthened, supported by resilient spending, robust investment and a labor market near full employment • Warsh said he is “hard-pressed” to describe financial conditions as restrictive, a view widely shared by the FOMC • The Fed raised rates to remove “a dose of accommodation” and align financial conditions with its objectives • Inflation remains “too high,” with summer data showing little meaningful improvement • With the labor market stable, price stability is now the Fed’s predominant focus • Warsh declined to signal another hike, saying he is “not in the forward-guidance business” • He said policy will respond to broader trends, calling dependence on individual data releases “dangerous” • Stronger growth, persistent inflation and geopolitical risks drove the unanimous decision • Warsh rejected claims that markets led the hike, stressing it was the Fed’s independent decision • He said the Fed does not need to weaken the labor market to bring inflation down News | Markets | YouTube

U.S. House to Consider Crypto Tax and Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bills Today According to Eleanor Terrett, although the Clarity Act may be stalled in the Senate, the House will continue considering crypto-related legislation today. At 10:00 a.m. ET, the House Ways and Means Committee will mark up a crypto tax bill, while the House Financial Services Committee will begin considering several bills, including the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill introduced by Rep. Nick Begich earlier this year. — link

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig: Agency Will Advance Crypto Rules Under Existing Statutory Authority U.S. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on X that yesterday’s Senate vote was unfortunate and that Americans deserve regulatory clarity, legal certainty and consumer protections in crypto asset markets. He said President Trump had promised to deliver a future-proof crypto asset regulatory market structure, adding that the CFTC would help advance it using its existing statutory authority. Selig added that the CFTC is ready to issue rules for the “new frontier of finance.” — link

Celsius Sues BitMEX 11 Days Before Exchange Shutdown, Seeking $495 Million Celsius’ bankruptcy estate sued entities linked to BitMEX in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York on Sept. 12. The complaint alleges fraud, market manipulation and wrongful liquidations during Bitcoin’s March 2020 crash, involving 6,360 BTC worth approximately $495 million at the time of filing. The case was brought by Blockchain Recovery Investment Consortium (BRIC) on behalf of Celsius. BitMEX is scheduled to stop trading on Sept. 23, while the allegations have not been established by the court. — link

Fed Raises Rates by 25 Bps to 3.75%–4.00%; 16 of 18 Officials See at Least One More Hike in 2026 Just In: The Federal Reserve’s FOMC voted unanimously, 12–0, to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, while continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system. The FOMC said the U.S. economy continues to expand at a solid pace, domestic spending remains resilient, productivity growth and capital investment are strong, and the labor market is broadly stable. Uncertainty remains elevated, in part due to geopolitical developments. Inflation remains elevated, and the Committee said the rate increase is intended to support a timelier return to its 2% target. Wall Street Journal reporter Nick Timiraos said 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more rate increase in 2026, while few projected rates to end 2027 below 4%. — link
